analyzed_vuln.description: `scanCFG` stores raw pointers to definition expressions in `DefinitionMap` (`exit.fBefore.set(var, e1)` and sentinel casting), where those expressions are owned by CFG/IR nodes that can later be replaced or removed during optimization. After such mutations, `ProgramUsage::get` calls `Variable::initialValue()` and dereferences a stale poisoned `unique_ptr` target, producing a use-after-poison. Root cause is unsafe lifetime/aliasing of expression-definition pointers propagated by dataflow, not `initialValue` itself.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Triggered during `SkRuntimeEffect::Make` compilation with optimization/control-flow analysis enabled. A crafted SkSL input that causes CFG/dataflow propagation plus expression/statement simplification (dead-assignment / replacement) leads `scanCFG` to retain definition pointers to expressions whose storage is later invalidated. Subsequent dead-variable analysis (`is_dead` -> `ProgramUsage::isDead` -> `ProgramUsage::get` -> `Variable::initialValue`) reads through the stale pointer and crashes.
